subject: High-priority: sudden token-deny spike after burst policy change — requires exec credit & rollback
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@aperturehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: support@aperturehealth.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 21:10:00 +0000
Subject: Production spike — 5xx and token denies since 20:45 UTC

Jonas / Monica,

We started seeing a sharp rise in end-user errors and latency around 20:50 UTC tonight. Symptoms: 35% of generative requests returning token-denied 429s and ~2x tail latency on the remaining successes. Affected service: Aperture Health clinical summarization (tenant id: AP-7721).

We've attached a small sample of failed request IDs and timestamps. Customers are reporting timeouts and degraded UX. This started immediately after the maintenance window. Can you confirm whether any quota/burst policy changes were deployed at 20:45 UTC?

Immediate ask: an estimate of impact, potential mitigation (temporary credits / rollback), and a time for a warp call. We're losing clinician confidence — need quick remediation.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of Integrations — Aperture Health
alex.turner@aperturehealth.com

Attachments: aperture-request-ids.csv (sample request ids), request-samples.jsonl (representative payloads)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 21:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — 5xx and token denies since 20:45 UTC

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the samples. Monica and Hannah, I'm looping you in to triage.

Quick notes / asks:
- Monica: please validate whether the tenant was hit by any credit / quota change on our end and pull the per-minute rejection histogram for AP-7721.
- Hannah: please check policy rollout logs around 20:40–21:00 UTC for any burst window updates or keying changes.
- Alex: can you confirm if Aperture pushed a client-side retry/parallelization change tonight?

I'll coordinate an emergency call if we confirm this is our change. Monica, if this looks like a policy regression, we should consider an immediate rollback and a short-term credit to avoid SLA penalties. Please keep me posted.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 21:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — 5xx and token denies since 20:45 UTC

Quick triage summary (initial):
- Confirmed: change deployed to burst-policy service (policy id bp-20260902-7) at 20:43 UTC.
- Observed behavior: burst window for several enterprise tenants was reduced from 65s -> 30s due to a rounding optimization intended to tighten cross-tenant fairness. That change caused earlier-than-expected enforcement for tenants whose traffic aligns with the minute boundary.
- Impact on AP-7721: immediate per-minute token denial surge when their short bursts coincide with the new window alignment. Rejection rate peaked at ~38% between 20:50–21:05 UTC.

I've attached the patch diff (burst_policy_diff.patch) and a sample of requests showing the rejection header. We have request IDs and timestamps in aperture-request-ids.csv and request payloads in request-samples.jsonl.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Rollback bp-20260902-7 to previous window behavior (fast).
2) Issue temporary emergency credit for AP-7721 to cover retries while we stabilize.
3) Open a postmortem entry and block this policy until compatibility tests added.

I'll start the rollback if Hannah gives the go-ahead.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: burst_policy_diff.patch, aperture-request-ids.csv, request-samples.jsonl

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 21:50:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production spike — technical root & recommended action

Initial findings from runtime logs and policy router: 
- Root cause: the bp-20260902-7 change introduced a windowing rounding change. For tenants with bursty traffic aligned to the previous boundary, requests are now bucketed into a shorter enforcement window, causing artificial token exhaustion.
- Secondary failure mode: fallback routing for degraded instances was erroneously routing AP-7721 to a lower-priority serving pool with stricter per-tenant caps. That magnified the rejection rate.
- Metrics: peak reject rate 38%, 95p latency from 220ms -> 480ms, customer error volume up 4x.

Immediate actionable plan (recommended):
A) Rollback bp-20260902-7 across regions (target: 10 minutes).
B) Apply an emergency per-tenant credit / temporary burst bump for AP-7721 for 4 hours to avoid retries causing cascading latency.
C) Route AP-7721 back to the verified priority pool and monitor for 60 minutes.
D) Notify customer and execs with monitoring dashboard link and ETA.

Risk: rollback is low-risk but requires coordination with infra change-control; routing fix requires a hotfix to the policy router config (safe but surgery required).

Please approve A+B so I can run the remediation steps. If approved, I'll call the rollback and monitor.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal SRE, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 22:05:00 +0000
Subject: Exec ask: approval for $30k emergency credit + immediate rollback of burst-policy bp-20260902-7

Marissa / Laura — immediate exec decision required. Summary: bp-20260902-7 rolled out at 20:43 UTC reduced burst windows; AP-7721 hit peak 38% reject rate and elevated latency. Customer-facing impact: significant clinical workflow delays; risk of churn and SLA breach.

Requested approvals:
- Approve immediate rollback of bp-20260902-7 across regions (Hannah has the rollback plan and estimates 10–15 min to complete).
- Approve a one-time emergency credit of $30,000 to Aperture Health (to cover retries and SLA unhappiness) while we stabilize. Finance/legal teams can reconcile later.
- Approve priority CS/Eng bridge and an immediate customer call (30 minutes).

Why $30k: conservative estimate based on observed retry cost, potential lost revenue, and to signal executive-level commitment. We should explicitly offer this to reduce escalation risk.

If approved, Hannah will execute rollback and Monica will lead the customer comms.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference
